title: UniPoolerV2.pool/quotePool size the zap from getReserves() without sync(): an unsynced token donation to the pair is absorbed in swap(), stranding non-dust phUSD on the pooler (229 phUSD on a 100k zap after a 0.5% donation) or reverting pending pool() with InsufficientLP, with the donation recoverable via skim() for gas only
borderlineNote: Medium would require sustained availability loss that matters: pool() delay does not affect users, funds, or the mint path, and keeper countermeasures (private RPC already recommended by L-22; sync() at top of pool()) are trivial. Re-weigh to Medium only if pool() latency becomes economically load-bearing (e.g., a time-sensitive peg defence relying on zaps).
description: UniPoolerV2.pool/quotePool size the zap from getReserves() without sync(): an unsynced token donation to the pair is absorbed in swap(), stranding non-dust phUSD on the pooler (229 phUSD on a 100k zap after a 0.5% donation) or reverting pending pool() with InsufficientLP, with the donation recoverable via skim() for gas only
impact: (a) Strand: 0.5% sUSDS donation -> 229.398 phUSD left on the pooler after a 100k zap (PoC). The phUSD is protocol-held, not lost; owner rescueERC20 recovers it. The attacker's donation (5,105.88 sUSDS, ~22x the stranded value) is absorbed into pair reserves owned ~100% by the pooler, so the protocol is net UP. (b) DoS: 2% donation -> pool() reverts UniPoolerV2__InsufficientLP(48746147894859096248178, 49179748976765704050059); attacker skim()s the donation back (gas-only, requires bundling or it is skimmed by any searcher). Dispatch/mint path unaffected (P9).
attackPath: 1. Attacker sees keeper pool(a, quote*0.99, quoteLP*0.99) in the public mempool
2. Bundles: transfer x sUSDS to pair (no sync) -> keeper tx -> pair.skim(attacker)
3. Keeper tx reverts InsufficientLP; attacker recovers x; repeat per keeper attempt
Alt: smaller x lets pool() succeed but strands phUSD (attacker forfeits x to LPs)
likelihood: low - zero-profit griefing; requires bundling a public keeper tx; defeated by private submission or a keeper-side pair.sync()/skim() before pool()
assumptions: Keeper submits publicly; pooler is ~100% LP post-cutover (strand case net-positive for protocol)
externalRequirements: Attacker willing to pay gas per griefed call with no return
severityJustification: No value leaves the protocol (strand is rescuable and paid for by the attacker at >= 22x; DoS is gas-only and permissionlessly neutralised by sync/skim). Availability impact is limited to delaying a keeper-only POL-compounding call; user mints are unaffected. C4 treats zero-profit, per-call griefing of a non-core keeper function with a trivial operational counter as Low, not Medium. The falsified spec claim is a real Law-2 defect, surfaced via faithfulness cross-reference.
recommendation: Call IUniswapV2Pair(pair).sync() (or skim to self) at the top of pool() before reading reserves; correct the NatSpec / story-048 claim.
ledgerMatch: None. Q-15 b4df4a252b (PromotionUniV2_Eth addLiquidity residual dust, by-design) is a different contract and mechanism (it is not reserve-desync).

evidence.engines: forge (suites C,D) + medusa (MedusaUniPoolerDonate), independent; tripwires 13/13 fire
evidence.strand: 1M sUSDS / 1.06M phUSD pool; 5,105.88 sUSDS (0.5%) transferred to pair; pool(100,000, quote*0.99) succeeds, leaves 229.398 phUSD on pooler (dust bound: tens of wei); phUSD only moves via owner rescueERC20
evidence.dos: 2% donation -> pool(a, quoteOut*0.99, quoteLP*0.99) reverts UniPoolerV2__InsufficientLP(48746147894859096248178, 49179748976765704050059); attacker skim()s the donation back -> repeatable for gas
evidence.control: phUSD donation leaves re-poolable sUSDS (not stranded); trade-only front-runs PASS P1/P4/P8

faithfulnessCrossRef.note: Falsifies story-048 / NatSpec claims that a front-run 'never [changes] the leftover' and that quotePool's expectedLP 'remains a valid floor' (true only for swap-style front-runs). story-048 is auto-complete. Filed under its security label L-25 at honest Low; spec-conformance report must cross-reference it (no separate F label, to avoid double-filing).
